themes_detail.label: Graffiti surge in Midwood
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 21 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 2.6 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 700% increase (z-score: 9.84)—suggesting a coordinated tagging campaign or enforcement gap in CD314.
evidence: 21 graffiti complaints this week vs. 2.6 weekly baseline (z-score: 9.84, severity: high)
Timeframe: THIS WEEK only, indicating acute rather than chronic issue
reporting_angles: Ground canvass of Midwood blocks to map graffiti clusters and identify if tagging is concentrated in specific neighborhoods or corridors
Interview DSNY about response times and resources allocated to graffiti removal in CD314 vs. citywide average

themes_detail.label: Street noise explosion this week
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 89 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 20.2 per week—a 340% spike (z-score: 4.56)—indicating a possible construction surge, nightlife cluster, or recurring event.
evidence: 89 street/sidewalk noise complaints this week vs. 20.2 weekly average (z-score: 4.56, severity: high)
Timing: THIS WEEK only suggests acute event or condition, not long-standing pattern
reporting_angles: Identify whether spike correlates with new construction permits filed (316 DOB filings in last 90 days, 235 alterations) or specific venues/events
Interview residents on affected blocks about type, timing, and source of noise; cross-reference with 311 complaint geotagging to identify noise hotspots

themes_detail.label: Illegal posting blitz—6300% spike
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints exploded to 8 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 0.1 per week—a 6300% spike (z-score: 23.81, highest statistical anomaly in dataset)—pointing to a coordinated poster campaign or removal service failure.
evidence: 8 illegal posting complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 23.81, highest severity: high)
6300% increase—extreme statistical anomaly suggesting sudden onset rather than gradual trend
Baseline so low (0.1/week) that any spike is dramatic; even small absolute numbers represent massive relative surge
reporting_angles: Photo canvass of commercial corridors (Coney Island Ave, Flatbush Ave, Ocean Parkway) to document what is being posted—political campaign, commercial, or nuisance ads
Contact DSNY/Sanitation to determine if illegal posting removal is understaffed or if a specific entity is behind the campaign

themes_detail.label: Encampment emergence in Midwood
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints jumped to 5 TWO WEEKS AGO from a baseline of 0.5 per week—a 900% spike (z-score: 4.5)—indicating new homelessness concentration or reduced outreach enforcement in the district.
evidence: 5 encampment complaints two weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 4.5, severity: high)
900% increase from baseline—significant shift in homelessness visibility or reporting
Signal is 2 weeks old; need to verify if trend persists into this week
reporting_angles: Identify specific blocks where encampments reported and interview nearby residents and business owners about duration, sanitation concerns, and safety impacts
Contact DSS/Homeless Services and NYPD to determine if there has been a service reduction, intake center closure, or policy change affecting placement in CD314

themes_detail.label: Water system failures spike (3 weeks old)
themes_detail.summary: Water system complaints spiked to 60 THREE WEEKS AGO from a baseline of 16 per week—a 275% increase (z-score: 5.02)—but timing suggests issue may have resolved; verify if still active.
evidence: 60 water system complaints three weeks ago vs. 16 weekly average (z-score: 5.02, severity: high)
Timing is 3 weeks old—spike may have subsided; need current data to determine if ongoing or resolved
reporting_angles: Check DEP records for main breaks, service interruptions, or boil water advisories issued in CD314 three weeks ago and verify if resolved
Follow up with residents in blocks with high water complaints to assess lingering water quality issues or recurring failures
